final_text:
Confirmed — 141.98.10.79:12132 is the only non-standard-port, non-TLS outbound connection in the capture, and everything else is domain-controller (172.16.1.4) traffic or legitimate Microsoft/CDN TLS services.

---

# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | `172.16.1.66` | Sole non-DC local host driving suspicious traffic; source of all C2 traffic |
| MAC | `00:1e:64:ec:f3:08` | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.16.1.66` → `arp.src.hw_mac`; matches `eth.src` on all frames from `172.16.1.66` |
| Windows hostname | `DESKTOP-SKBR25F` | NBNS Workstation/Server service records for `172.16.1.66`; also self-reported inside the C2 beacon payload |
| Logged-in user | `ccollier` | Kerberos `CNameString` for AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic between `172.16.1.66` and DC `172.16.1.4`; also self-reported inside the C2 beacon payload |
| Domain | `wiresharkworkshop.online` | DNS queries for `_ldap._tcp...wiresharkworkshop.online`, `WIRESHARK-WS-DC.wiresharkworkshop.online` (DC at `172.16.1.4`, NBNS name `WIRESHARK-WS-DC`) |

## Malware Family

**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential-stealer, commonly delivered by fake-invoice/malspam campaigns). **Attribution: signature-confirmed** — the malware names itself explicitly in cleartext inside its own C2 protocol: TCP stream 83 (`172.16.1.66:49754 <-> 141.98.10.79:12132`) carries repeated beacons of the form:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender|<b64 active-window>|1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

This is STRRAT's known plaintext "ping" beacon format (pipe-delimited: literal string `STRRAT`, build/campaign ID, hostname, username, OS, AV product, base64-encoded active window title, malware version `1.6`, country, "Not Installed" flag, idle timer). No IDS/Suricata alert export was provided alongside this pcap, so attribution rests on this protocol content rather than a signature hit, but the malware is self-identifying — this is as strong as behavioral attribution gets.

- Beacon interval: ~5 seconds, first seen 2024-07-30 06:40:07 +0400 (t+78s), last seen 2024-07-30 06:48:34 +0400 (t+585.7s, end of capture) — beaconing was still active when the capture ended.
- Build/campaign ID: `1BE8292C`
- Reported version: `1.6`
- Reported AV: Windows Defender (Not Installed = AV not disabled/tampered per this field)
- Decoded active-window samples exfiltrated in the beacon (base64 field): `Home`, `Documents`, `Program Manager`, and `pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint` — the last suggests the user had a PowerPoint file named "pounds-formula" open in Compatibility Mode around the time of infection, a plausible phishing-lure document name, though the lure itself was not captured (SMTP/HTTP delivery of the file is outside this pcap's timeframe).

**Delivery-chain observation (circumstantial, not confirmed):** Immediately before the C2 beacon started, the host made back-to-back TLS connections to `github.com`/`objects.githubusercontent.com` (t=63.9–70.9s, ~833 KB) and `repo1.maven.org` (t=63.9–73.8s, ~8.9 MB), both legitimate-CDN-certificate-backed (verified via TLS certificate CN — DigiCert cert for GitHub, GlobalSign cert for Sonatype/Maven). STRRAT is Java-based and its loaders are known to fetch a portable JRE from exactly this kind of legitimate infrastructure before launching. All traffic here was TLS-encrypted, so no filename or payload could be recovered from the pcap; this is noted as behavioral context, not a hard IOC, since GitHub/Maven Central are legitimate services being abused, not malicious infrastructure themselves.

## Indicators of Compromise

```json

  "victim": {
    "ip": "172.16.1.66",
    "mac": "00:1e:64:ec:f3:08",
    "hostname": "DESKTOP-SKBR25F",
    "user": "ccollier"
  },
  "malware_family": "STRRAT",
  "attribution_confidence": "signature-confirmed",
  "iocs": [
    {
      "type": "c2_endpoint",
      "value": "141.98.10.79:12132",
      "evidence": "tcp.stream==83, 172.16.1.66:49754 <-> 141.98.10.79:12132, plaintext repeated pipe-delimited 'ping|STRRAT|...' beacons from 2024-07-30T06:40:07+0400 through end of capture (06:48:34+0400), ~5s interval, no TLS handshake on this port"
    }
  ],
  "benign_context": [
    {"note": "github.com / objects.githubusercontent.com (185.199.110.133) and repo1.maven.org (199.232.196.209) — legitimate, cert-verified CDN/repo infrastructure contacted via TLS just before the C2 beacon started; likely abused as a JRE-download source by the STRRAT loader, but no malicious content or filename could be recovered from encrypted traffic"},
    {"note": "www.msftconnecttest.com, mobile/v20/v10.events.data.microsoft.com, client.wns.windows.com, login.microsoftonline.com, autodiscover-s.outlook.com, officeapps.live.com, officeclient.microsoft.com, ecs.office.com, metadata.templates.cdn.office.net — standard Windows/Office/M365 telemetry and connectivity checks"},
    {"note": "www.bing.com, th.bing.com, assets.msn.com, api.msn.com, www.msn.com, img-s-msn-com.akamaized.net, arc.msn.com, ecn.dev.virtualearth.net, go.microsoft.com, g.live.com, oneclient.sfx.ms, config.edge.skype.com, default.exp-tas.com, msedge.api.cdp.microsoft.com, javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com, settings-win.data.microsoft.com — standard Edge/MSN/Windows browsing and update background noise"},
    {"note": "ip-api.com GET /json/ (208.95.112.1) at t=78.0s — IP geolocation lookup; timing coincides with STRRAT startup (STRRAT performs a geo-IP lookup on launch to populate its 'US:United States' beacon field) but this is a legitimate public API and the request itself is not malicious traffic"},
    {"note": "172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC) — the domain controller; all LDAP/Kerberos/DCERPC/SMB traffic to it is normal AD domain-join/auth activity for wiresharkworkshop.online"}
  ],
  "incident_summary": "The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user ccollier on wiresharkworkshop.online, is infected with STRRAT v1.6 (campaign/build ID 1BE8292C). The malware began beaconing in plaintext to its C2 server at 141.98.10.79:12132 roughly nine minutes into the capture and was still actively beaconing every ~5 seconds when the capture ended, exfiltrating host fingerprint data and the active foreground window title on each ping. The beacon itself named the malware family, so attribution did not require an external signature or the internet. No cleartext delivery artifact (dropper file name or hash) was captured; TLS-encrypted connections to GitHub and Maven Central immediately preceding the first beacon are consistent with STRRAT's known JRE-download loader behavior but could not be confirmed further without decryption."
}
```

**Recommended immediate actions:** isolate `172.16.1.66` from the network, block outbound `141.98.10.79:12132` at the perimeter, reset `ccollier`'s domain credentials (STRRAT is a credential stealer), and pull EDR/local telemetry from the host to recover the actual dropper/jar file and confirm the delivery vector (this pcap alone does not contain it).
